Web developers in Atlanta are not hard to find. What is hard to find is one who talks to a business of one: a barber, a caterer, a mobile detailer, a tax preparer with a client list and a phone. Most of the web design companies in Atlanta show case studies for firms with staff and budgets, and their prices sit behind a discovery call. Dominion Web Design Pro is an Atlanta web design option built the other way around: prices printed, a free demo before you pay, every page written by hand, and the site yours to keep.

Dominion Web Design Pro is a Black-owned business. Maurice Johnson owns it, and he is the person who writes and builds each site, from Big Sandy in East Texas. We work with Atlanta businesses remotely and will not pretend to have an Atlanta address. What we can offer is a straight price and a real site you can look at first.

Web design in Atlanta, GA starts with who actually owns the businesses

Metro Atlanta is big and still growing. The Atlanta Regional Commission estimated 5,339,164 people in its 11-county region in April 2026, after adding 53,690 residents in a year. Inside that region sits one of the country's largest concentrations of Black business ownership. LendingTree has ranked metro Atlanta first for its share of Black-owned businesses four years running, among the 100 metros with the most Black-owned businesses. In its latest study, which uses 2023 Census data, 10.7% of the metro's businesses with employees are Black-owned, against 3.4% nationally. Fayetteville, North Carolina and Washington, D.C. came next.

Those figures count businesses with payroll. Behind them are many more one-person operations: barbers in the West End, caterers working out of a shared kitchen, braiders, personal trainers in Midtown, mobile mechanics who work the I-285 loop. The Atlanta Wealth Building Initiative has reported a wide gap in what these businesses are worth: the average Black-owned business in Atlanta valued at about $58,085, against $658,264 for the average white-owned one. A business at that scale cannot carry a five-figure website and a monthly retainer, so the agencies never call. That is a pricing problem, not a quality problem.

Atlanta's business corridors, and what each one asks of a website

Atlanta has a long record of neighborhood commerce. Auburn Avenue, the heart of the Sweet Auburn district just east of downtown, was the economic center of Black Atlanta for most of the twentieth century; in 1956 Fortune magazine called it "the richest Negro street in the world." The district was designated a National Historic Landmark in 1976. A business street depends on being found, and today people look first on a phone.

The newer corridors work the same way. The Atlanta BeltLine is planned as a 22-mile loop through 45 neighborhoods. Its Eastside Trail, lined with restaurants and Ponce City Market, runs past Old Fourth Ward and Virginia-Highland, and the Westside Trail reaches historic neighborhoods such as the West End. The visitor who walked past a shop on Saturday still searches its name on Monday.

On the south and west sides, Invest Atlanta's Small Business Improvement Grant program has offered tenants and commercial property owners up to $50,000 for building improvements in seven of the city's tax allocation districts, including Campbellton Road, Hollowell-ML King and Metropolitan Parkway. The Invest Atlanta board approves the grants in rounds, so check with Invest Atlanta for when applications are open.

The kinds of Atlanta businesses a website helps most

Food comes first: restaurants, catering, bakeries and food trucks from Old Fourth Ward to the Westside. Plenty of them run on an Instagram account and a phone number in a bio link. That works until a customer types "catering near me" into Google and finds someone else. Keep the social accounts, and give customers one link you own.

Health and personal care is just as large. LendingTree's study found that 26.2% of Black-owned businesses nationwide were in health care and social assistance in 2023: home care agencies, therapists, child care providers, medical billing. Those owners sell trust, and a prospective client checks the site before calling.

Service trades round it out. A plumber in Southwest Atlanta or a cleaning company covering Buckhead and Sandy Springs is searched by job and neighborhood. One page per service, the areas covered and a tap-to-call number at the top answer those searches in a way a social profile cannot.

Why local search decides who gets the call

Google says its local results rest mainly on three things: relevance, meaning how well a business matches the search; distance from the person searching; and prominence, meaning how well known the business is, drawing on links, articles, directories and reviews. Google also says a business's position in its regular web results counts toward prominence, which is why search engine basics still apply to local businesses.

In a metro of more than five million people, relevance is the factor a small business can most directly control. An Atlanta web designer who writes a real page for each service you offer and each area you cover gives Google something specific to match. That is the reasoning behind SEO web design and behind the city pages in our Pro and Agency packages. Nobody can promise you a ranking, and we will not; what we can do is make your site clearly about what you do and where you do it.

Free help for Atlanta small businesses

  • Invest AtlantaThe city's development authority runs Small Business Resource Centers through its ATLinBusiness program, with no-cost one-on-one consulting, in person or online, for businesses inside the city of Atlanta. It also runs the improvement grants described above.
  • Metro Atlanta ChamberThe regional chamber, founded in 1859, works on the economy, talent and community of a 29-county region. Its Atlanta Metro Export Challenge has given small and mid-sized metro companies reimbursement grants of $5,000 toward international growth costs.
  • UGA Small Business Development CenterThe University of Georgia's SBDC network gives no-cost consulting through metro Atlanta offices, including one at Morehouse College, and works with partners such as Georgia State University.
  • SCORE AtlantaVolunteer mentors and workshops, a resource partner of the U.S. Small Business Administration.

When you are ready for the website, bring the four questions above to every web designer you talk to.

Common questions

How much does a web design company in Atlanta charge a small business?

Many Atlanta agencies do not publish prices, and custom builds can run into the thousands before any monthly fees. Dominion Web Design Pro prints its prices: $497 for a 5-page Starter site, $997 for Pro and $1,997 for Agency, one time. Hosting, maintenance and updates are $49 a month, or included while you keep the AI agent.

Is there a Black-owned web design company that works with Atlanta businesses?

Dominion Web Design Pro is Black-owned. Maurice Johnson owns the business and writes and builds the sites himself, from Big Sandy in East Texas, and he works with Atlanta owners remotely. We are not an Atlanta firm and will not pretend to be one. If buying from a Black-owned business matters to you, our Black-owned web design page explains who we are and how to check any company's ownership claim.

Do you do WordPress web design for Atlanta businesses?

The packages are sold by what you get (pages written for your business, the search setup, the contact form), not by a platform name. Maurice writes each page and builds the site, and with hosting and maintenance in place you send a message when something needs to change and the change gets made. If you need WordPress, for example because your staff edits a WordPress site every week, say so when you ask for the demo and you will get a straight answer before you buy, or an Atlanta WordPress specialist may suit you better.

How do I find the best web designers in Atlanta for my business?

The best one for you is the one whose price, process and finished work fit a business your size. Ask every designer for the price in dollars, who owns the site and the domain, what a change costs six months from now, and to see a site built for a business like yours. A designer who will not answer all four is telling you something. Hold us to the same four questions.

Can web developers outside Atlanta build a good site for an Atlanta business?

Yes, for most small businesses. Website work happens by phone, email and shared links whether the developer sits in Midtown or in Texas. What you give up is meeting in person. If you want a clear, fast site at a printed price, location matters much less, and the free demo lets you judge the work before you spend anything.

See your website before you pay for it

Give us your business name and what you do, and a demo site gets built for you to look at on your own phone. If you like it, pick a package. If you do not, you have spent nothing but the minute it took to look.
